contracts: Rust ActionControl has an opt-in activation-on-press mode used by selectors. Ordinary actions retain release activation. On-press activation requires enabled, visible, inside and trigger admission, consumes pending pointer state before callbacks and prevents late release or drag from activating again. Mode changes cancel pending input.

SelectState owns the last real popup-close timestamp. Pointer opens require a strictly greater interval than the native kMinimumTimeBetweenButtonClicks supplied by the platform adapter (currently 100ms); keyboard/AX opens bypass that pointer guard, matching Combobox. Stale close callbacks cannot update the current guard or collapse a newer popup.

Closing or dismissing a real native popup records close time even when selection has already marked the Rust model collapsed. Dismissing an absent popup does not move the close clock. Existing selected keys, prefix matching, empty selection and menu generation checks remain.

Opening reveals an offscreen anchor before building the popup and guards against a runner synchronously removed by scheduling. Selector scheduling synchronously closes an expanded native popup if its anchor becomes hidden or fully clipped, before GPU work is coalesced. A late mouse release cannot reopen it. Native menu/focus/IME/window/AX and domain services remain adapters.

The shared popup test now asserts the actual MenuController exists immediately after root mouse press in both modes, before release. It retains AX/Down opening, live expanded/collapsed states and unchanged value after cancellation. The Rust-only branch opens a real popup using the keyboard, clips its anchor, returns and dispatches late release with no reopening; AX then reveals the offscreen anchor and opens it again.

Five additional Rust tests cover ordinary versus press activation, disabled/miss/nontrigger/invisible admission, mode transitions, strict guard boundaries and backwards clock values, keyboard bypass, stale callbacks, selected native popup dismissal and absent-popup observations. Existing profile/import/preferences/tools and shared action outcomes remain asserted.
